title: VM NUMA Alignment
exclusions: Reports a powered-on VM whose qualified esxtop `N%L` (percentage of VM memory on the local NUMA node) averages at or below Broadcom's published 80% troubleshooting threshold in three consecutive complete five-minute buckets. It preserves `NRMEM` and `MEMSZ` in vendor-labeled megabytes for context but does not substitute `mem.llSwapUsed`: Splunk documents that counter as host-cache swap, not NUMA remote memory. Low locality is a performance-review signal, not proof of incorrect vNUMA topology, application impact, root cause, or a required configuration change. ESXi can intentionally span wide VMs and dynamically rebalance home nodes/memory; some workloads benefit from bandwidth across nodes. The rule excludes non-NUMA hosts, powered-off VMs, user worlds/resource pools not mapped to a VM, unsupported/renamed esxtop fields, guest NUMA visibility, CPU locality, affinity, Hot Add, scheduler demand, and application latency except as corroboration. Threshold persistence, critical <=50%, and bucket schedule are documented choices. Missing samples/VMs and failed collection are health defects. No VM sizing, affinity, topology, Hot Add, migration, or power action occurs.
evidence: After deployment retain authoritative vCenter/host/VM/NUMA topology and workload ownership inventory; ESXi hardware/build, VM hardware/version, vCPU/memory/Hot Add/advanced-setting state; reviewed `Get-EsxTop` collector and field map/hash; VCF PowerCLI/ESXi/vCenter/Splunk versions and privileges; effective scripted-input/JSON configuration; raw N%L/NRMEM/MEMSZ samples and topology mapping; expected powered-on VM, non-NUMA exclusion, sample cadence, world-to-VM identity, schema, duplicate, timestamp, and collector health; `vmware_vm_sustained_low_numa_locality` definition, ACL, schedule, dispatch/results/delivery/disposition; application and host contention evidence; and dated 80/50 boundary, three-bucket, gap, duplicate, stale, migration, and mapping tests. Preserve raw units, bucket values/counts, host/VM IDs, interval, source health, topology/change context, and decision. This documentation-only review created no esxtop sample, event, alert, benchmark, VM change, or production validation evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In a fixed closed 30-minute fixture, ingest valid samples for one stable VM/host in three adjacent five-minute buckets with average local_memory_pct 80, 79, and 78. Expect one warning result because each bucket is <=80 and exactly adjacent. Repeat with 50, 49, and 48 and expect critical because the three-bucket minimum is <=50. Assert bucket times, average/minimum locality, sample count, raw NRMEM/MEMSZ summaries, host/VM identity, thresholds, and UC ID.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero rows when any of three buckets averages above 80; for only one/two breached buckets; three breached buckets with a five-minute gap; invalid percentage outside 0-100; negative NRMEM/MEMSZ; NRMEM greater than MEMSZ without an approved field interpretation; non-VM entity; failed/partial collector status; blank stable identity; future/stale sample; duplicate sample; or an older host placement superseded after vMotion. Separate health must expose missing expected powered-on VM/bucket, world mapping failure, non-NUMA host, counter-layout drift, and collector failure.

dataSources: A reviewed VCF PowerCLI `Get-EsxTop` collector (or separately qualified esxtop/resxtop batch adapter) discovers the deployed counter/topology schema, maps VM worlds to stable vCenter `vm_moid`, and emits one JSON sample per powered-on VM at an approved interval no slower than five minutes to local `index=vmware`, `sourcetype=vmware:esxtop_numa`. Required fields are `vcenter`, `host_moid`, `host`, `vm_moid`, `vm_name`, `entity_type=virtual_machine`, numeric `local_memory_pct` from esxtop N%L, nonnegative `remote_memory_mb` from NRMEM, positive `memory_size_mb` from MEMSZ, integer `sample_epoch`, unique `sample_id`, `collector_status=ok`, and collector/field-map version. Broadcom labels NUMA values megabytes and N%L percentage. Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics `mem.llSwapUsed` is KB of host-cache swap and is not used.
app: A locally maintained `TA_vmware_esxtop_numa` with reviewed `Get-EsxTop`/topology adapter and JSON source type, plus an observability app for expected-VM/counter health, saved search, dashboard, tests, routing, and runbook. Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics (5089) is useful for general VM memory/CPU context but its documented llSwap metrics do not replace this NUMA locality contract.
spl:
index=vmware sourcetype="vmware:esxtop_numa" collector_status="ok" entity_type="virtual_machine" earliest=-30m@m latest=-5m@m
| eval vcenter=lower(trim(vcenter)), host_moid=trim(host_moid), esxi_host=lower(trim(host)), vm_moid=trim(vm_moid), vm_name=trim(vm_name), local_memory_pct=tonumber(local_memory_pct), remote_memory_mb=tonumber(remote_memory_mb), memory_size_mb=tonumber(memory_size_mb), sample_epoch=tonumber(sample_epoch), sample_id=trim(sample_id)
| where len(vcenter)>0 AND len(host_moid)>0 AND len(esxi_host)>0 AND len(vm_moid)>0 AND len(vm_name)>0 AND local_memory_pct>=0 AND local_memory_pct<=100 AND remote_memory_mb>=0 AND memory_size_mb>0 AND remote_memory_mb<=memory_size_mb AND isnotnull(sample_epoch) AND len(sample_id)>0
| eval _time=sample_epoch
| dedup sample_id
| bin _time span=5m
| stats avg(local_memory_pct) as bucket_local_pct avg(remote_memory_mb) as avg_remote_memory_mb avg(memory_size_mb) as avg_memory_size_mb count as samples by _time vcenter host_moid esxi_host vm_moid vm_name
| where bucket_local_pct<=80
| sort 0 vcenter vm_moid esxi_host _time
| streamstats current=f window=2 list(_time) as prior_breach_times list(bucket_local_pct) as prior_local_pcts by vcenter vm_moid esxi_host
| eval prior_old=tonumber(mvindex(prior_breach_times,0)), prior_new=tonumber(mvindex(prior_breach_times,1))
| where mvcount(prior_breach_times)=2 AND prior_new-prior_old=300 AND _time-prior_new=300
| eval three_bucket_min_pct=min(bucket_local_pct,tonumber(mvindex(prior_local_pcts,0)),tonumber(mvindex(prior_local_pcts,1))), three_bucket_avg_pct=round((bucket_local_pct+tonumber(mvindex(prior_local_pcts,0))+tonumber(mvindex(prior_local_pcts,1)))/3,3), local_severity=if(three_bucket_min_pct<=50,"critical","warning"), locality_threshold_pct=80, persistence_minutes=15, use_case="UC-2.1.40", breach_end_utc=strftime(_time+300,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"), breach_start_utc=strftime(prior_old,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
| table vcenter host_moid esxi_host vm_moid vm_name local_severity three_bucket_min_pct three_bucket_avg_pct bucket_local_pct avg_remote_memory_mb avg_memory_size_mb samples breach_start_utc breach_end_utc locality_threshold_pct persistence_minutes use_case
| sort 0 three_bucket_min_pct vcenter esxi_host vm_name
description: Monitors sustained NUMA memory locality for powered-on VMs using the vendor esxtop N%L statistic. It reports three consecutive five-minute buckets at or below Broadcom's 80% troubleshooting value and retains remote and configured-memory context, giving performance engineers a precise review signal without equating host-cache swap or VM width with NUMA misalignment.
value: Remote NUMA memory can increase access latency for sensitive workloads, but ESXi dynamically manages placement and wide VMs are not inherently wrong. A persistence-aware locality signal helps teams correlate real low-locality periods with topology, contention, migration, and application performance before considering risky sizing or advanced-setting changes.
implementation: Qualify `Get-EsxTop` counter/topology names on each supported ESXi build, map VM worlds to stable identities, and collect N%L/NRMEM/MEMSZ every five minutes or faster with independent completeness health. Save the delayed three-bucket search, validate exact 80/50 boundaries and gaps, compare with live esxtop and workload latency, and route only sustained results to VMware/performance owners. Prefer rightsizing/default scheduler behavior; change advanced NUMA settings only after controlled benchmark and rollback.
visualization: Use a per-VM N%L timechart with 80%/50% lines; a table with host/VM, three-bucket min/average, NRMEM/MEMSZ MB, interval, source health, topology/sizing, workload latency, change, and disposition; host/cluster distributions; and separate expected-VM, non-NUMA, world-map, counter-layout, sample-gap, and collector-health panels. Never graph llSwap as remote NUMA memory.
schema: Purpose-built normalized esxtop VM NUMA locality samples with stable vCenter identity
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable. The Performance CIM and documented VMware Metrics fields do not preserve esxtop N%L, NRMEM, MEMSZ, world-to-VM mapping, counter-layout version, and collector completeness required by this rule.

knownFalsePositives:
A result is sustained low locality under the qualified counter contract; impact and corrective action still require evidence:

1. **Wide VM by design** — ESXi can split a VM across NUMA nodes and expose vNUMA so the guest manages locality. Confirm guest/application NUMA behavior and latency before calling it misconfigured.

2. **Transient rebalance or vMotion settling** — ESXi can change home nodes and migrate memory. The 15-minute persistence removes brief transitions, but correlate migration and later recovery.

3. **Bandwidth-oriented workload** — some workloads benefit from memory bandwidth across nodes even with lower locality. Use application benchmark/SLO evidence rather than a universal remediation.

4. **Host contention or placement pressure** — low N%L can reflect aggregate demand rather than VM topology. Inspect host node free memory, co-tenants, DRS, reservations, and workload timing.

5. **Manual affinity or advanced settings** — intentional settings can constrain scheduler behavior. Confirm owner/change and benchmark; stale overrides are candidates for removal, not automatic edits.

6. **VM identity/world mapping change** — vMotion, restart, or world reuse can attach samples incorrectly if mapping is weak. Require stable moid plus host/sample topology and surface mapping failures.

7. **Counter-layout/version drift** — esxtop fields can vary by release/interface. If N%L/NRMEM/MEMSZ mapping is not proven, fail source health instead of emitting zero or swapped units.

8. **Duplicate samples** — repeated routes can bias bucket averages. Deduplicate unique sample ID and repair the collector.

Suppress only exact vCenter/VM moid/host context with workload evidence, owner, reason, start, and finite expiry. Never suppress expected-VM/sample, world-map, counter-layout, or collector-health reporting.
mitreAttack: N/A (VMware performance monitoring; no adversary behavior asserted)
detectionType: Three consecutive five-minute low-NUMA-locality buckets from esxtop N%L
reviewer: Source-backed documentation-only editorial review; production VMware performance and Splunk validation pending

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and measurement semantics

Assign VMware performance, hardware, guest/application, Splunk, and change owners. Inventory NUMA-capable hosts by sockets/nodes/cores/memory and every governed powered-on VM by stable moid, workload/SLO, vCPU/memory, hardware version, cores-per-socket/automatic topology, Hot Add, affinity/advanced settings, DRS placement, and owner. Record non-NUMA hosts and unsupported builds explicitly.

Broadcom defines esxtop N%L as percentage of VM memory local to its NUMA node, NRMEM as current remote memory in MB, and MEMSZ as VM physical/configured memory in MB. Broadcom troubleshooting guidance flags N%L <=80%. This implementation requires three complete five-minute buckets and locally classifies <=50% critical. It does not use `mem.llSwapUsed`; Splunk documents that metric as host-cache swap in KB.

## Step 1 — Collect and qualify esxtop data

Use supported VCF PowerCLI `Get-EsxTop`, which exposes counters and topology. On every supported build, first enumerate CounterInfo and TopologyInfo; version-control the exact field and instance mapping. Map VM world/group to stable vCenter VM moid and current host. Never map by display name alone. A separately approved esxtop/resxtop batch adapter may be used, but preserve source labels and units.

Emit one JSON sample per powered-on VM every five minutes or faster with unique sample ID and field-map version. Reject resource pools/user worlds, ambiguous mappings, non-NUMA hosts, missing fields, and partial host polls to health. Configure a scripted input/HEC path with explicit JSON source type. Compare samples simultaneously with interactive esxtop memory panel (enable NUMA fields), PowerCLI raw counter output, vCenter identity, and VM configuration. Prove 0-100 N%L and nonnegative NRMEM/MEMSZ.

Build expected powered-on VM/sample health from inventory: missing host/VM/bucket, duplicate sample, stale/future time, interval drift, counter-layout change, mapping ambiguity, impossible values, collector/API failure, and cardinality shift. Preserve collector overhead; reduce scope or interval safely if ESXi/vCenter impact is material.

## Step 2 — Create and understand the search

Save sidecar `spl` as `vmware_vm_sustained_low_numa_locality` and run every five minutes after measured ingest delay. The closed event-time window `earliest=-30m@m latest=-5m@m` excludes the newest five minutes. Normalize and validate identity/values, replace `_time` with source sample epoch, deduplicate sample ID, and average samples into five-minute buckets.

Only buckets with average N%L <=80 remain. After stable ascending sort, `streamstats` retains the prior two breached bucket times/values. Exactly 300-second adjacency twice proves three consecutive breached buckets; a missing or healthy middle bucket prevents a result. Three-bucket min determines <=50 critical; three-bucket average is context. Multiple results can occur during a long breach, so throttle alerting by VM/host while preserving continuing and worsening evidence.

## Step 3 — Validate boundaries, gaps, and identity

Use fixed fixtures at 100, 80.001, 80, 79.999, 50.001, 50, 0; multiple samples per bucket; one/two/three/four breaches; healthy and missing middle buckets; host/VM change; duplicate sample; stale/future/partial status; invalid percentage/MB; NRMEM>MEMSZ; non-VM entity; ambiguous world; and rerun. Assert exact start/end and no llSwap fields.

In a nonproduction NUMA host, run a bounded NUMA-sensitive benchmark approved by workload/hardware owners. Capture esxtop, guest NUMA tools, vCenter topology, host-node free memory, CPU/memory contention, and application latency. Exercise vMotion and safe sizing/topology variants one at a time. Do not force production remote memory or apply undocumented advanced settings. Keep draft until counter mapping, overhead, and workload correlation are signed off.

## Step 4 — Diagnose before changing topology

Alert title should say `Sustained low VM NUMA memory locality`. Include VM/host stable IDs, three-bucket locality, NRMEM/MEMSZ MB, topology/sizing/Hot Add/affinity, DRS/migration/change context, host-node pressure, application SLO, source health, and raw links. Verify live esxtop and mapping; determine whether VM is wide and vNUMA exposed; inspect guest/app NUMA awareness; examine host contention/DRS; correlate performance; review manual overrides; then classify expected design, transient placement, contention, sizing/topology issue, collector defect, or unresolved.

Prefer removing unnecessary vCPU/memory and relying on supported automatic topology before advanced overrides, subject to workload testing. Never automatically resize, change cores per socket, affinity, NUMA advanced settings, Hot Add, vMotion, or power state. Such changes can require downtime and can degrade performance. Close only after workload owner validates impact/action, source health is good, and fresh locality/application evidence is acceptable.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot

- **No NUMA fields:** verify host NUMA capability, CounterInfo/TopologyInfo, permissions, build support, collector field map, and raw esxtop display.
- **NRMEM/MEMSZ but no N%L:** do not derive an unqualified ratio if semantics differ; qualify the exact formula/build or fail health.
- **All values zero/100:** compare live esxtop and known remote-memory lab control; inspect wrong entity/field and numeric parsing.
- **VM names collide:** map world to vCenter moid and host at each sample; never aggregate name-only.
- **Results after vMotion:** split by host and verify source time/mapping; new-host placement starts a new sequence.
- **llSwap correlates:** host-cache swapping is separate memory pressure context, not proof of NUMA remote memory.
- **Frequent gaps:** inspect collector duration/overhead, API session, scheduling, ingestion delay, and expected-sample health; do not weaken adjacency.

Retention and response thresholds follow local performance policy. This signal initiates evidence-based tuning; it does not prescribe universal NUMA configuration.
grandmaExplanation: We watch whether a virtual machine keeps most of its memory close to the processors using it. If memory stays far away for several checks, performance experts investigate before changing the machine's size or layout.
hardware: Powered-on VMs on NUMA-capable ESXi hosts whose esxtop NUMA fields and VM-world topology have been qualified for the exact release/build.
